items.title: Finnish-led project to receive EUR 9.55 million in EU funding
items.summary: The European Commission has awarded EUR 9.55 million in funding to a Finnish-led project aimed at reinforcing submarine cable repair capacity. The project is coordinated by the Finnish National Emergency Supply Agency and involves partners from Finland, Sweden and Estonia. The funding was awarded under the Connecting Europe Facility (CEF) Digital programme.

items.summary: Europeiska kommissionen beviljade 9,55 miljoner euro i stöd till ett projekt som leds av Finland och som ska stärka kapaciteten för reparation av undervattenskablar. Tor releases emergency update amid ongoing DDoS attack
items.summary: “This release comes in rapid response to the ongoing DDoS attack on the network, which has affected most relay operators,” the Tor Project said in its release announcement. The project said a massive ongoing flood of client circuits has overwhelmed relays across the privacy network, causing a problem that has been difficult to address. The project says this update includes a security fix to improve relay defenses against denial-of-service attacks. "One fix in particular is especially important for relay DoS defenses related to IPv6 handling," explains the project.

items.title: QUIC and Covert: Novel HTTP/3-Powered RATs Target Southeast Asian Governments
items.summary: Over a nine-month period, we observed the attackers behind the activity consistently refining their capabilities to meet evolving operational needs. This campaign’s tradecraft features three particularly advanced capabilities: Covert HTTP/3 (QUIC) C2 communications: An early adoption of HTTP/3 over UDP, providing a highly efficient command and control channel that may bypass traditional TCP-optimized deep packet inspection. An operational safety switch: PerfectPioneer RAT features a built-in validation engine that actively blocks remote operators from executing noisy or destructive commands that could trigger environment security alerts. Multi-vector heuristic camouflage: KUKURAT employs a custom spoofing engine that generates synthetic, benign-looking network, registry and file activity. By manipulating the behavioral baseline of the endpoint, it can successfully obscure indicators of compromise within a vast volume of artificial noise.

items.title: COLD RELIC: A Case Study in Impersonation and Compromise
items.summary: While Google Threat Intelligence Group (GTIG) has tracked and disrupted COLD RELIC phishing campaigns since 2015, recent Mandiant incident response investigations have uncovered critical new insights into the group’s social engineering and post-compromise tradecraft. We are sharing this end-to-end analysis—along with actionable detection and hardening guidance—to help organizations defend against COLD RELIC’s ongoing use of stolen pretexts, localized residential proxies, and cross-cloud identity abuse. As part of our efforts to thwart this threat actor, we issue Government-backed attack alerts when we detect COLD RELIC targeting Google accounts. COLD RELIC remains an active threat; GTIG has observed evidence of new phishing operations as recently as November 2026.

items.title: High volume phishing campaign uses Microsoft 365 outage lures to target multiple industry sectors
items.summary: On November 13, 2026, Microsoft Threat Intelligence observed a coordinated, high-volume phishing campaign targeting organizations across multiple sectors worldwide. The threat actors used phishing emails disguised as legitimate Microsoft 365 service-health notifications to lure recipients into clicking a malicious link. The messages created a false sense of urgency by claiming that emails had been held during a service disruption and would be deleted within 24 hours unless the recipient took action to restore them. This is consistent with historical attacker campaigns which continuously look for notable global events to exploit in their social engineering lures.

items.title: Why threat hunting should matter to every board
items.summary: Boards should have confidence that their organisation can detect and investigate emerging cyber threats, including activity that existing security alerts may miss. This blog is for boards of organisations that monitor their systems for cyber threats, either themselves or through a third-party provider. It explains why threat hunting matters as threats evolve, and how boards can support their organisation to learn from what it finds and turn those insights into stronger cyber defences.

items.title: Kyber­hyökkäyksen uhriksi joutunut kauppias kertoo soitosta aamuyöllä – tällaista minuuttipeliä kyberiskuista on tullut
items.summary: Kauppias Mariia Jernmark lähti heti kaupalle. Paikan päällä selvisi, että kylmälaitteet olivat kuumentuneet, ja tuotteita oli mennyt pilalle erittäin suuria määriä. Helsingin Lauttasaaressa sijaitsevan K-market Oliivin kylmälaitteiden säädöt menivät vinksalleen marraskuun alussa. Jernmark ja kaupan henkilökunta ryhtyivät hävittämään pilaantuneita tuotteita ja täyttämään hyllyjä uudelleen. Kun selvisi, että kyseessä saattaa olla jonkinlainen kyberhyökkäys, tunne oli epätodellinen.

items.title: Widespread service outages at major U.S. banks appear to be over
items.summary: Customers at JPMorgan Chase, Bank of America, U.S. Bank and other major financial institutions reported service outages on Monday, according to Downdetector.com. Chase also said in a social media post that a software bug in its systems affected other institutions "when we were party to a transaction involving other banks." The issue is not systemic, the bank added.

items.title: World's Largest Brands Infected With Malware Via Optimizely
items.summary: On 16 November 2026, malicious JavaScript was served to visitors of 178 organisations through the Optimizely Web experimentation platform. The list includes some of the most visited sites in the world: Zoom, the BBC, CNN, Salesforce, GitLab, IKEA, HSBC, Equifax, Air France-KLM, Ledger and Peacock. The malware was a multi-purpose kit. It swapped cryptocurrency wallet addresses for the attacker's, skimmed payment cards, stole cookies and screenshots, and on iPhones and iPads it delivered the Coruna and DarkSword iOS exploit kits. Crypto has already been stolen, with verified transactions to the attackers.

items.title: Java4Shell
items.summary: A memory-corruption vulnerability in OpenJDK's Base64 decoder. A remote attacker with no credentials can overwrite heap memory, read it in the style of Heartbleed, and reach remote code execution. Our initial testing demonstrated remote code execution in the following widely deployed Java applications, in their default configs. Pre-auth RCE: Keycloak Atlassian Jira Atlassian Confluence JFrog Artifactory Jenkins PingFederate Post-auth RCE: Apache Kafka Broker Apache Solr Elasticsearch Gerrit Netflix Spinnaker The lists are non-exhaustive. We also demonstrated RCE in sample applications built on widely used frameworks, including Apache Struts and Spring Boot. One thing to note about this vulnerability is that there is no universal exploit. Depending on how Base64 is used and how the application works, different steps may be required for exploitation. Java4Shell affects OpenJDK from version 17.0.6 or newer. Because the vulnerable code is hardware-specific, Java4Shell also requires an x86-64 processor with AVX-512 VBMI support. ARM64 CPUs are not affected. All Java users should update immediately. You can also mitigate Java4Shell by starting OpenJDK with either: -XX:-UseBASE64Intrinsics to disable hardware-accelerated Base64 encoding and decoding, or -XX:UseAVX=2 to disable AVX-512. Apply this flag only on x86-64 hosts. OpenJDK on ARM doesn't recognize it and will fail to start.
items.summary_html:
A memory-corruption vulnerability in OpenJDK's Base64 decoder. A remote attacker with no credentials can overwrite heap memory, read it in the style of Heartbleed, and reach remote code execution.

Our initial testing demonstrated remote code execution in the following widely deployed Java applications, in their default configs.

Pre-auth RCE:

Keycloak
Atlassian Jira
Atlassian Confluence
JFrog Artifactory
Jenkins
PingFederate
Post-auth RCE:

Apache Kafka Broker
Apache Solr
Elasticsearch
Gerrit
Netflix Spinnaker
The lists are non-exhaustive. We also demonstrated RCE in sample applications built on widely used frameworks, including Apache Struts and Spring Boot.

One thing to note about this vulnerability is that there is no universal exploit. Depending on how Base64 is used and how the application works, different steps may be required for exploitation.

Java4Shell affects OpenJDK from version 17.0.6 or newer.

Because the vulnerable code is hardware-specific, Java4Shell also requires an x86-64 processor with AVX-512 VBMI support. ARM64 CPUs are not affected.

All Java users should update immediately.

You can also mitigate Java4Shell by starting OpenJDK with either:

-XX:-UseBASE64Intrinsics to disable hardware-accelerated Base64 encoding and decoding, or
-XX:UseAVX=2 to disable AVX-512. Apply this flag only on x86-64 hosts. OpenJDK on ARM doesn't recognize it and will fail to start.
